decisions.executionNote: Orient both wrists progressively downward while moving toward separate near-side objects; maintain elbow-up continuity and inspect geometry before descent.
Retry initial downward wrist rotation with much smaller increments after zero-execution IK rejection.
Continue to near-vertical approach above the two wooden toys without descending into the table.
Fine-align and lower open grippers over the wooden toys. Left toy will require central staging for the right arm rather than crossing arms.
Complete vertical alignment, descend the last few centimeters and close on the two toys; retention remains unverified until lifting.
Lift both closed grippers gently to verify whether the toys are retained, replanning from observed contact-limited poses.
Both toys appear lifted. Carry right toy toward red basket and left toy toward a clear central-front staging point, keeping arms separated.
Use smaller forward steps and slightly lower right wrist to preserve reach margin at red basket; bring left toy to central-front staging.
Right toy appears to have slipped beside the basket; return open to recover it. Lower left toy at center-front for later right-arm retrieval.
Release the staged wooden toy and withdraw left toward the near watch. Back the right gripper away from basket contact before a new pickup.
Align left fingers over the near watch; carefully approach the right wooden toy from above, keeping the underlying chocolate separate.
Close on near watch and recoverable wooden toy, then lift vertically to check retention and confirm chocolate stays on the table.
Raise retained right toy well clear of basket lip. Reposition left grasp toward the near side of the watch band after the missed pickup.
Close on the realigned watch and test lift. Advance the held right toy slowly above the red basket with increased lip clearance.
Both objects are visibly retained. Carry watch toward white basket; lower and tilt right wrist slightly forward to gain basket clearance without approaching full extension.
Release right wooden toy over red basket and withdraw toward staged toy. Advance the retained watch inside the white basket before opening.
Finish placing the watch inside white basket and open. Withdraw right arm in smaller increments from the successfully deposited wooden toy toward the staged one.
Watch is visibly released into white basket. Clear left arm back into its workspace while right approaches the center-front staged wooden toy.
The staged toy shifted slightly. Keep right EE at the center boundary and gently cant fingers toward it while backing into alignment; left remains clear.
Test retention of the staged toy with a slow lift and slight movement into the right workspace; left stays still and clear.
Staged toy was not retained and is now left of center. Clear right arm outward while left approaches to restage it safely; no arm crossing.
Approach shifted toy with left arm and first chocolate with right; correct wrist cant and keep open through alignment.
Grasp and lift the toy with left arm; align right gripper across the chocolate's narrow dimension before closing.
Restage the held toy toward the center with a modest wrist cant while keeping left EE left of center. Fine-align and close right on one chocolate only.
Set the toy down at the center boundary and release gently; lift the single held chocolate clear before carrying it to the middle basket.
Withdraw left from the restaged toy. Carry retained chocolate toward blue basket with modest forward tilt and conservative reach.
Advance chocolate fully over the middle basket in small increments, maintaining reach margin and keeping it closed until placement alignment is visible.
Release the chocolate over the blue basket at the current reachable pose, then retreat gently before selecting another object.
Chocolate is released inside blue basket. Ease away from the near-extension pose with smaller initial retreat steps, approaching the remaining watch.
Square the right wrist downward and align the fingers at the near half of the remaining watch band, based on the previous successful watch grasp.
Pinch the near portion of the second watch and lift to verify retention before transferring it toward the left arm.
Watch was not retained. Move forward to center the band between the pads, descend carefully and retry the pinch.
Lift the newly pinched watch and bring it to a central staging area with wrist cant; keep the right EE on its own side and left arm stationary.
Set the retained watch onto a clear spot just left of the center boundary for left-arm pickup; keep left stationary until right withdraws.
Withdraw right outward from the released watch; approach the staged watch with left only after separation grows, keeping both arms in their own workspace.
Fine-align left over the transferred watch and right over the remaining chocolate, descending open in separate workspaces.
Close left on the staged watch and right on the remaining chocolate, then lift slowly to verify each object is retained.
Both objects are visibly held. Carry watch toward white basket and chocolate toward blue basket with gentle forward wrist tilt for reach and rim clearance.
Advance watch inside the white basket and release it. Move chocolate carefully farther over blue basket before opening, with small reach-limited increments.
Release the second chocolate into blue basket, then ease right away toward the last toy. Start returning the empty left arm toward its origin.
Return left close to its initial pose while right approaches the last toy at the center boundary, correcting wrist orientation without crossing arms.
Finish left reset with small continuity-safe increments. Align right fingers around the last toy without pushing it toward the center edge.
Close around the last wooden toy and test a slow vertical lift; left remains at its initial open-gripper pose.
Last toy is visibly retained. Carry it through the right workspace toward red basket, lifting above the lip and removing the sideways cant.
Advance retained final toy above the red basket with forward wrist tilt and cautious lowering, maintaining separation and reach margin.
Final toy slipped against the basket lip. Reapproach it open from above; next transfer will use greater vertical clearance and forward reach from wrist tilt.
Center the right pads on the fallen toy's body, close, then test a short vertical lift before approaching the basket again.
Lift the retained toy vertically to clear the red basket's lip before any forward transport, then begin gentle forward tilt.
Carry the raised toy over the red basket using small forward increments and more wrist tilt, keeping it above the rim before release.
Release the final toy above the red basket interior, pause for settling, then withdraw the empty right arm toward its origin.
All six objects now appear in their assigned baskets. Return empty right arm smoothly toward its starting pose and correct small left reset residual.
Continue the empty right arm reset at reduced increments near the initial configuration; both grippers remain open and baskets undisturbed.
